\section[a drogaria]{a drogaria — the household goods shop (cleaning things, paint)}

\label{lesson:PT-C449-drogaria}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for the scratch card, then the Portuguese for to leaf through.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: a drogaria}
\textbf{a drogaria} — \textquotedblleft{}the household goods shop (cleaning things, paint)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Comprei lâmpadas e sacos do lixo na drogaria.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I bought light bulbs and bin bags at the household shop.}
\end{quote}

Not a chemist: medicine is at \emph{a farmácia}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{drogaria} is built on \emph{droga} with \emph{-aria}; \emph{droga} came from French \emph{drogue} (EtymDB), probably from Low German \emph{droge} 'dry (goods)'.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{a drogaria}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{a drogaria}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{a drogaria}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for the scratch card, then the Portuguese for to leaf through, then say \emph{a drogaria} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does a drogaria mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The household goods shop (cleaning things, paint)\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[a retrosaria]{a retrosaria — the haberdashery}

\label{lesson:PT-C449-retrosaria}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for to leaf through, then the Portuguese for the household goods shop.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: a retrosaria}
\textbf{a retrosaria} — \textquotedblleft{}the haberdashery\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Na retrosaria encontrei botões para o casaco.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{At the haberdashery I found buttons for my coat.}
\end{quote}

Thread, buttons, zips and ribbons.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{retrosaria} is built on \emph{retrós} 'silk thread' with \emph{-aria}; the origin of \emph{retrós} is not settled, and EtymDB has no entry for it.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[a perfumaria]{a perfumaria — the perfume shop}

\label{lesson:PT-C449-perfumaria}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for the household goods shop, then the Portuguese for the haberdashery.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: a perfumaria}
\textbf{a perfumaria} — \textquotedblleft{}the perfume shop\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Ela trabalha numa perfumaria do centro comercial.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{She works in a perfume shop in the shopping centre.}
\end{quote}

Built on \emph{o perfume}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{perfumaria} is built on \emph{perfume}, which probably came through Italian or French from Latin \emph{per} 'through' and \emph{fūmus} 'smoke' (Lewis \& Short): first a scent rising in smoke.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for the household goods shop, then the Portuguese for the haberdashery, then say \emph{a perfumaria} again
\end{itemize}

\section[a ervanária]{a ervanária — the herbalist's shop}

\label{lesson:PT-C449-ervanaria}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for the haberdashery, then the Portuguese for the perfume shop.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: a ervanária}
\textbf{a ervanária} — \textquotedblleft{}the herbalist's shop\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Na ervanária vendem chás para dormir.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{At the herbalist's they sell teas to help you sleep.}
\end{quote}

Built on \emph{a erva}, the herb.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{ervanária} is built on \emph{erva} 'herb, grass', which is inherited from Latin \emph{herba} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[a ourivesaria]{a ourivesaria — the jeweller's shop}

\label{lesson:PT-C449-ourivesaria}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for the perfume shop, then the Portuguese for the herbalist's shop.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: a ourivesaria}
\textbf{a ourivesaria} — \textquotedblleft{}the jeweller's shop\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
O anel veio de uma ourivesaria antiga.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The ring came from an old jeweller's.}
\end{quote}

\emph{O ourives} — the goldsmith.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{ourivesaria} is built on \emph{ourives} 'goldsmith' with \emph{-aria} (EtymDB); \emph{ourives} is inherited from Latin \emph{aurificem}, from \emph{aurum} 'gold' and \emph{facere} 'to make'.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
